proposed_normalization.action_convention: For each task id T, propose action:complete-desert-T. Each action has one completion milestone desert_T_task_complete, is non-repeatable, and records only the verified task interaction. Combat tasks must use a player-confirmed encounter outcome and never fabricate a kill or head drop.
edge_patterns: prerequisite skill, quest, item, minigame, and location nodes -> task action (requires)
all same-tier task milestones plus previous diary-tier node -> tier claim action (requires)
tier claim action -> diary-tier node, amulet, lamp, and tier-specific capability nodes (produces)
only historical/existing transport and minigame nodes -> task action (references); do not duplicate their full mechanics
proposed_normalization.lamp_boundary: Each claim action creates a fixed player-chosen lamp entitlement. It must not choose a recipient skill or convert lamp XP into a skill-XP transition without explicit account input.
state_boundaries: Daily Nardah teleport counts and individual Pharaoh's sceptre charges are capability data; the current package does not propose unrestricted repeat actions.
Pollnivneach rooftop XP/mark modifiers, random Hunter/Thieving outcomes, and combat encounters remain reported mechanics or observation-gated transitions.
No KQ kill, KQ head, Pyramid Plunder artefact, or combat supply is granted by this package.

conflicts_and_unknowns.resolution: Do not use the 2015 reward blog's 4/5/6/8 sceptre capacities. Current Wiki sources consistently record 10/25/50/100, and the package uses those live values.

The current Diary page reports roughly 14% more XP and 25% more marks. Preserve the wording as a capability until the engine supports course-reward modifiers; do not derive an exact per-lap XP formula here.

The diary task requires the mounted/stuffed head, not merely a KQ kill. The normal 1/128 head and the tattered-head 256-kill guarantee are kept as an acquisition boundary, never a deterministic item effect.

Ropes are recorded as consumed-or-placed when a task explicitly requires first access. Their persistent world-state behavior belongs to the existing transport/minigame model; hard-tier permanent-rope reward is stated separately.
